brief.headline: Ask Silk Polypack for ₹205/kg on laminates (market-fair bottom) and 15 extra days' credit to free up ₹320 cash for us.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹205/kg for our pharma/ORS sachet laminate.
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking price for pharma/ORS sachet laminate sits in a ₹205–305/kg band, typical ₹250/kg. Our target hits the fair-band floor — still reasonable but captures maximum value for us. The import price for BOPET film substrate is 171.60 ₹/kg, so ₹205/kg leaves them room for conversion and margin.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Push their payment terms from 30 days after receipt to 45 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹320 cash for us (15 extra days on our ₹7775 annual spend).

brief.financialLeverage: Silk Polypack publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or cash position. Our annual spend with them is only ₹7775 — tiny, so we aren't a make-or-break customer for them. That limits how hard we can push on price alone. But the fact that we have two strong listed alternates (Huhtamaki and UFLEX, both proven converters at scale) gives us real walk-away power. The play is to qualify one of those alternates now and use that as leverage: we'll split the volume unless Silk Polypack meets our price and terms.

evidence.point: Our annual spend with Silk Polypack is tiny.
Market asking price for pharma/ORS sachet laminate runs a fair band.
Import price for BOPET film substrate (the raw material) is much lower.
Pushing payment from 30 to 45 days frees up working cash for us.
Huhtamaki India is already a tiny FDC supplier and a listed flexible-packaging converter.
evidence.figure: proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

evidence.point: UFLEX is a listed flexibles giant that makes both film and does conversion.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — proven and scalable for laminate sachets; strong fallback if Silk Polypack won't move.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film substrate and conversion — can handle our volume at scale and offers end-to-end supply security.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates — credible second source (though private, revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health score D 31/100, so check stability before you RFQ).

risks: Silk Polypack has no public financials, so we can't see if they're healthy or struggling — watch for any signs of delivery delays or quality slip that hint at cash trouble.
Our ₹7775 spend is so small we have almost no leverage from volume alone — the threat of moving to Huhtamaki or UFLEX is our real card, so line one of them up before this meeting.

If Silk Polypack is a pure reseller (not the converter), pushing them to ₹205/kg may squeeze out their margin entirely — ask who actually makes the laminate and consider going direct to that converter.

The market-ask verdict says ₹205–305/kg is 'market-fair (top of fair band)' — our ₹205/kg target is aggressive (bottom of the band); be ready for pushback and have ₹220–230/kg as a fallback that still saves us money.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're reviewing all our laminate suppliers this quarter — we'd like to lock in ₹205/kg and 45-day terms with you, but we're also talking to Huhtamaki and UFLEX to make sure we have a second qualified source in place.
